description: Homes come in three tiers (hut, house, hall) with room for 2, 4 and 6.
notes: Partly there: Villheim homes have beds and upgrade by design family; no tier with its own wants.

description: Each tier wants more from the store: any food; then meat or honey and mead; then meat, mead, coal and bread.
notes: Partly there: food variety by village stage. Bread needs barley (Plains); use the biome's best food instead.

description: Needs are taken from the store each round, one unit per two residents of the tier.
notes: Villheim would check each morning per household, against the village chest.

feature: Moving out when needs are unmet
description: Each round a need is unmet, every home of that tier loses one resident down to one.
notes: Already there in Villheim's form: 10 days without bed, food or safety and a villager leaves for a neighbour.

feature: Homes fill while needs are met
description: Homes gain residents each round their needs are met and they are connected by road.
notes: Already there in Villheim's form: newcomers arrive for a free bed, by day.

feature: Upgrade only a full, content home
description: A home can go up a tier only when it is full and its needs are met.
notes: New rule for Growth.cs: upgrades today do not look at needs.

description: The old building comes down and the next tier's design goes up on the same spot.
notes: Already there: rebuild as the next level of the family, old building taken down first.

description: Boxes show the room the next tier needs before the player confirms.
notes: UI for the player's view; a ghost of the next building could still show villagers' plans (Later ideas).

description: Residents pay 1, 3 or 8 coins a minute by tier.
notes: Might not fit: Villheim has no coin income loop. Could become a small tithe to the chest from content homes.

description: A research makes residents eat 15% less food.
notes: Might fit as a storehouse effect: a cellar design lowers food use.

description: Settlers regain health slowly and are left alone by wildlife.
notes: Already there: healing by real food. Wildlife ignoring villagers does not fit.

description: Up to 15 residents walk the roads between buildings as decoration.
notes: Already there: strolls and free time.

description: Walkers keep 0.55 m to the right of the road's middle so two can pass.
notes: New and small: offset the path points by half a metre.

description: Work buildings take a worker from the free residents of the right tier.
notes: Already there in Villheim's form: trades from six villagers.

description: Idle residents fell marked trees and clear stumps, rocks and bushes at half speed.
notes: Already there: villagers clear sites. Player marking is not wanted.

description: Swamp buildings stand on a stone plinth and cost 20% more.
notes: Only when Swamp villages come.

description: Clan villages keep their last eight pieces of news (built, upgraded, paved).
notes: Already there: news list on the hearth, carried by visitors.

description: Heroes have a name from Norse lists and a class with its own description.
notes: Fits the hero idea; Villheim has names and personalities already.

description: Warnings name the compass direction of the danger.
notes: New and small: a {direction} fill-in for raid lines.

description: Woodcutters fell trees around their hut and carry the wood to the store.
notes: Already there: woodcutters and the gathering order.

description: Drops first, then felled logs near the last tree, then fresh trees.
notes: Already there: the CLAUDE.md gathering order.

description: A target that cannot be reached is skipped for 90 s.
notes: Already there from the VikingColonies and Innangard study.

description: Workers carry up to 20 goods before going to the store; research adds more.
notes: Already there in some form; check the number.

description: Foragers gather berries, mushrooms and flint near their hut.
notes: Already there: foraging by carers.

description: Hunters shoot deer and boar and bring meat and hides.
notes: Already there: protectors hunt when food is low.

description: With no game in reach a hunter walks to the edge of his range, stalks, and returns with a rolled catch.
notes: New: an off-screen trip when no animal is near.

description: Game comes less often and trips are longer when the land around the cabin is built over.
notes: New: count built cells 15 to 50 m out.

description: Stonecutters break rocks into stone.
notes: Already there: miners.

description: Miners break nearby copper, tin, silver and scrap veins.
notes: New: a mining outpost (WORLD_LIFE step 4 lists mining camps).

description: Raw meat becomes cooked meat, venison cooked venison, with a recipe switch.
notes: Already there in Villheim's form: real cooking at the cooking station.

description: Bee hives make honey on a timer.
notes: Fits: crafted bee hives are allowed; only wild hives are kept out (Tyler, 2026-11-08). Needs a queen bee from a wild hive.

description: Wood is burnt into coal.
notes: New: run the vanilla charcoal_kiln from the chest, as the smith runs his station.

description: Honey and berries become minor healing mead.
notes: New: vanilla cauldron then fermenter; mead is a home need.

description: Farmers plant the vanilla crop on a field behind the farm and harvest it.
notes: Partly there: berry and mushroom rows; seeds (carrots in the Black Forest) are planned.

description: Barley becomes flour, flour becomes bread.
notes: Plains only (windmill, oven); later biomes.

description: Wood and flint become spears and shields for soldiers.
notes: Already there: the smith makes each tier's set at the real station.

description: Scrap iron and silver ore are smelted with coal; iron gear is forged.
notes: New for later tiers: a village forge with smelter; WORLD_LIFE step 7.

description: Miners dig silver using wood for pit props; silver gear and necklaces are made.
notes: Mountain villages only; far off.

description: Fishermen row out on a raft and bring in fish.
notes: Harbour designs exist (15); a fisher trade would need a boat or shore fishing.

description: Villagers feed the game's own stations from the chest and bring the output back.
notes: Villheim's version of the mod's timed production; the smith is the pattern.

description: Each product has a keep amount; work stops when the store holds it.
notes: Fits the rule that nobody harvests when nothing is needed.

description: Each work building says what it lacks (no road, missing wood, enough in stock).
notes: New: hover text and vh village line per station.

description: Unloaded work buildings add goods at a rate from the trees or rocks counted around them.
notes: Partly there: outposts add a daily amount. Could extend to the home village while no player is near.

description: The store shows how much of each good is made and used per minute and when it runs out.
notes: Could feed the notice board's Needed sign.

description: A research gives 50% more storage.
notes: Villheim's storehouse adds chests; nothing to take.

feature: Piece by piece from real parts
description: Houses appear one piece at a time from real building pieces.
notes: Already there and further: a builder at each piece, ground first, support order. The mod spawns on a timer with no worker.

description: Pieces go up ordered by height, the building's anchor last.
notes: Already there.

description: Total build time is 0.12 s a piece, 8 to 75 s.
notes: Villheim times by builder and skill; nothing to take.

description: The piece's own place effect plays on every third piece.
notes: Check that Villheim plays the place effect per piece.

description: The building's centre, yaw and half size are kept on its anchor piece.
notes: Already there in Villheim's form: plots on the hearth.

description: A plan of every piece lets repair put back only what is missing, in its place.
notes: Already there: repairs from the design.

description: A repair costs the building's price times the share of pieces missing.
notes: Already there in Villheim's form: each piece paid from the chest.

description: A small annex design is placed beside a work building and raises its rate.
notes: New: decor stages (d#) could add a lean-to or shed beside a workshop.

description: Standing buildings are restyled piece by piece in the new age's materials.
notes: New: MaterialSwap only swaps down; an up direction when the stage cap rises.

description: One 2 m wood wall is replaced by a stack of log walls at set heights.
notes: Detail for the up-swap: one piece may become several.

description: Blueprint and vbuild files from a folder become building designs.
notes: Already there: both formats read.

description: A text file maps each building name to its list of blueprint files; a template lists them all.
notes: New: a Tyler-editable mapping from kind or base ID to design files.

description: A design becomes a building type by its anchor piece (bed for homes, chest for stores); one is added if missing.
notes: Useful as a check: every home has a bed, every workshop its station.

description: Each type has a fixed plot; bigger designs are squeezed to it with a warning.
notes: Partly there: plot size from the design. The warning list is useful in the design review.

description: Food, mead and wards in community blueprints are never built.
notes: Already there in some form; check wards (PrivateArea) are dropped.

description: Each blueprint's picture is rendered from its real pieces once and cached.
notes: Partly there: the lab draws designs; PNGs for saved stages are on the roadmap.

description: Placement says which piece is in the way.
notes: Useful in the log when a plot is refused.

description: Trees whose crowns hang over a new plot are felled first.
notes: New and small: check tree crowns as well as trunks.

description: Small saplings on a plot are cleared by the site.
notes: Check Villheim's site clearing for saplings.

description: Finished houses are combined for drawing; 36 to 56 fps in a test town.
notes: From the author's post. Performance idea for grown villages; risky with WearNTear.

feature: No support checks on mod pieces
description: Mod-built pieces skip the game's structural and rain cover checks to save time.
notes: Might not fit: Villheim wants real support. Only for very large villages.

description: A village plan takes one of four shapes: star round a plaza, grid town, street village, crossroads.
notes: New: a street plan per culture or village type.

description: Plots line both sides of each road, sized to fit, with some double plots for special buildings.
notes: Partly there: buildings along roads after Millénaire.

description: The hall sits at the head of the plaza or in the middle of a star village.
notes: Already there: longhouse round the hearth.

description: Each plot gets a role (house, workshop for a good the village makes, special) and a wanted level.
notes: Partly there: one pending project and growth tiers.

description: Wants rise on the world clock; the real village is built to match when a player is near.
notes: Partly there: caravans and outposts already work as records.

description: Some plots get a fence round the back and sides; the front stays open and shared sides are skipped.
notes: Gives rules for proposal 26 (back yards).

description: Wood stacks, stone piles, barrels, log benches or a beehive in the yard, by what the village makes.
notes: Vanilla pieces only. A crafted bee hive is fine; wild hives are not.

description: Main streets are paved once the village reaches tier 3.
notes: New: repaint main paths with the paved type at a stage.

description: The plaza is painted as a disc of paved or dirt ground.
notes: Already there in some form: the hearth area is cleared.

description: A village is placed in a forest look (trees kept between plots) or a clearing.
notes: New: keep trees between plots for woodland villages.

description: Buildings without a road to a store do not grow, pay or produce.
notes: Partly there: daily door check plans a path. A work penalty would be new.

description: Connection is tested by a flood fill over road cells from the building to a store.
notes: Already there in Villheim's form: path network on the hearth.

description: Rings show the reach of the skald's fire, meadery and watchtower.
notes: Player UI; might not fit.

description: A marked area of 8 to 64 m is levelled over time with soft edges; trees on it go to the store.
notes: New for the village core before its first ring of plots.

description: Thriving clans send people and coins to found a new village.
notes: Already there.

description: Terrain may change up to 100 m from its original height.
notes: Check: LevelPad allows 16 m, the game may clamp at 8 m when it applies the heightmap.

description: Heights are written per 1 m point into the zone's terrain data with a target function.
notes: Already there: LevelPad writes level deltas.

description: Free villagers walk to the next spot, swing for 3 s, and that spot is levelled.
notes: Partly there: sites are levelled at once. Spot work makes it visible.

description: Levelling leaves ground within 2.5 m of any building piece so nothing loses its footing.
notes: New and small.

description: Ground under a finished building is levelled to its floor with a soft run-out.
notes: Already there: repairs level under floors first.

description: Levelled areas blend to the old ground with a smoothstep over a band of 4 to 14 m by slope.
notes: Partly there: LevelPad has a smooth radius. Band by slope is new.

description: Levelling never writes inside another building's footprint.
notes: New and small.

description: A path's profile is cut or filled so it never climbs more than 0.33 m per metre.
notes: New: A* today only prices slope.

description: Where a fill would be deeper than 2.2 m or over water, a wood or stone bridge is built.
notes: New: small plank bridges from vanilla pieces, paid from the chest.

description: Where a cut would be deeper than 5.6 m, the path goes through a stone tunnel.
notes: Might not fit villages; route around instead.

description: A path cut into a hill is refitted when the ground on it changes.
notes: New: refit a path when a site levelling touches it.

description: A river bed is carved along a line with a water level that never rises downstream.
notes: New: the method suits streams by villages.

description: River and lake water is a mesh with the game's water material and WaterVolume boxes, so it can be swum.
notes: New: runtime objects rebuilt on zone load.

description: Water lines are stored on each zone's terrain ZDO so every client builds the same water.
notes: Pattern for any per-zone village data.

description: Steep drops in a river become falls.
notes: Comes with the river method.

description: A polygon of water at a set level, also above sea level.
notes: Fish ponds or mill ponds by a village.

description: Dug ground below sea level stays dry where the sea is masked.
notes: Do not take: editor only.

description: A zone whose saved terrain loaded late is loaded again so its changes show.
notes: Worth checking if any Villheim zone shows its original ground.

description: After terrain changes, trees and bushes in the area are snapped to the new height.
notes: New and small: avoid floating bushes after levelling.

description: Grass is redrawn in the changed area after each write.
notes: Check Villheim resets ClutterSystem grass.

description: Dirt and paved roads are painted along a free line.
notes: Already there in Villheim's form: paths painted by villagers.

description: Paths laid as slabs or planks along a curve, following the ground.
notes: New: plank walks in swamp villages, stone in later stages.

feature: Fences, torches and tree avenues along a line
description: Fences, walls, hedges, torches or trees placed along a path at set spacing.
notes: Partly there: signposts. Torches along the main street and lamp posts on trails (Living Factions) fit.

description: New worlds are generated with lower hills.
notes: Do not take: changes the whole world.

description: Lumberjacks plant saplings on stumps of felled trees first.
notes: Partly there: one sapling per tree, 8 to 25 m beyond the village.

description: Around each lumber hut the number of trees is kept at 10 to 30.
notes: Partly there: groves plant when under 25 trees within 60 m.

description: Beech, oak and birch in the Meadows, pine and fir in the Black Forest, fir in mountains, birch in the Plains.
notes: Already there: same kind as felled, else the biome's tree.

description: A forager nearby halves tree regrowth and sapling grow time.
notes: New and small.

description: Pickables near a forager respawn sooner, and the scarcest bush kind is planted.
notes: New and small.

description: New rocks appear around a quarry up to a target.
notes: Might not fit: invents stone. Needs Tyler's decision.

description: Deer and boar spawn around a hunting cabin up to 2 to 8, fewer when the land is built over.
notes: Needs a decision: spawning animals near a village.

description: One ore vein grows back every 8 minutes up to the starting count.
notes: Might not fit: invents ore.

description: Clearing an area takes the stumps too.
notes: Already there in some form; check stumps on sites.

description: New lairs appear further out each age, up to a set number.
notes: Fits proposal 41 (bandit camps that grow).

description: One store holds all goods; workers bring everything there.
notes: Already there: the village chest.

description: A trader with a cart stays four minutes with two goods to buy and one to sell.
notes: Already there: pedlars.

description: Goods sold at worth x0.8 and bought at x1.4.
notes: Already there: store prices.

description: Clans keep stock of what they make, use what they want, and trade by caravan or ship.
notes: Partly there: caravans carry surplus to neighbours.

description: Gifts and trade agreements raise a clan's relation.
notes: Partly there: gifts to the chest count in the player record. Gifts between villages are new.

description: A beaten or friendly clan pays coins every minute.
notes: Might not fit.

description: Ships sail a found sea path between harbour and clan on their own.
notes: Might not fit soon: needs harbours and boats.

description: An item key decides what stays with the player and what goes to the store.
notes: Do not take: city view feature.

description: A banner counts down to the raid and shows its direction.
notes: Partly there: warning at dusk. Direction and arrival time are new.

feature: Raids walk from a real place
description: A raid is a record that walks from a clan or tribe toward the town and becomes real near it.
notes: New: raid party as a caravan kind from a camp location.

description: Five or more raiders split 60/40, the second wave 45 s later.
notes: New and small.

description: Each age adds stronger enemies (elite greydwarfs, draugr, wolves, goblins).
notes: Partly there: size by tier, elites later. Per boss stage is new.

description: Clans across the water land with longships.
notes: Might not fit.

description: A raid that wins burns one of the six buildings nearest it to a ruin.
notes: New: ties to fire and ruins.

description: Two to four archers on a tower shoot raiders and monsters within 45 m.
notes: New: protectors on a watchtower design at night.

description: Walls drawn round the town that raiders must break.
notes: Already there: the fence ring that grows.

description: Idle soldiers attack raiders near town; one button sends everyone.
notes: Already there: protectors defend; the horn.

description: A squad walks between two points and fights what it meets.
notes: Partly there: night watch and protectors at the edge.

description: An alarm when deathsquitos fly over the walls; towers aim at them first.
notes: Plains villages only.

description: Villagers' arrows and swings never damage their own buildings.
notes: Check: protectors fighting near walls.

description: Three heroes a day at the tavern: warrior, berserker, hunter or seeress, hired for coins with a wage.

description: Heroes follow through portals, into dungeons and aboard ships.

description: Experience from kills, up to level 10, with more health and damage each level.

description: A hero wears or wields an item the player hands over.

description: A fallen hero comes back after 10 minutes, or at once for coins.

description: A völva heals everyone within 15 m.

description: Free residents are trained into squads of up to 8 with gear from the store.

description: The army marches to a camp and fights or is auto-resolved.
notes: Do not take.

description: A party goes into a crypt or cave type and returns with its loot list.

notes: New and small.

description: Allied clans do not declare war on members of the alliance.

description: Scouts walk the fog and find clans, traders, lairs and dungeons.

description: The sky turns red and a horde comes.
